lines.text: In the Catalogue, press / to jump straight to the search box. No mouse required.
Every project here was found on at least one awesome-list. The Atlas merges them, so you only read each project once.
Meet Nib, Archie's old cursor. It collects letters. Keep an eye on the headings.
Ctrl+K (or Cmd+K) in the Catalogue opens Jump to, for going anywhere in a few keystrokes.
When three or more awesome-lists name the same project independently, it lands on the Named by three or more lists shelf.
Meet Posy, a sticky note with opinions. If a card gets a note, it's a compliment.
Not sure what you want yet? Discover is the browsing aisle: fresh finds, hidden gems and deep cuts.
Every project in the Atlas has a page of its own, with the lists that named it. Even the weird ones.
Meet Lumen, a moth who thinks the spotlight is the moon. She may pose for it.
Archie and friends too chatty? The Quiet mode button in the Catalogue hushes the lot. They won't sulk. Much.
Hidden gems are projects two or more lists named that are still under 500 stars. Get in early.
Meet Oh-Four, a shy little ghost. If something peeks over the search button, just wave.
Collections are hand-picked sets for a job, like playlists for repositories. Start with First setup.
The little dot beside a card's age is how recently the project was pushed to: hot, warm, stale or cold at a glance.
Meet Quack, the debugging duck. Quack says nothing. Archie explains everything. Bugs get fixed.
Prefer plain text? The whole Atlas is also a Markdown mega-list on GitHub, greppable to the last line.
The spotlight changes every day, so a different project gets its turn at the top of the page each morning.
Nib is back. It says its font is nearly finished. It needs just one more letter. It always needs one more letter.
When Archie is up in the masthead, put some music on and try Dance with me. He keeps time to what he hears.
There's a shelf just for projects that run natively on Windows, no WSL required.
Posy's here again, with a fresh pad of notes. Archie has asked her to go easy on the adhesive.
Archie can be poked. Poke him a few times in a row and see what happens. He's load-bearing, but not that fragile.
Want nothing to leave your machine? The Local only collection gathers projects that run without a cloud.
Lumen drifted in overnight. She has written a poem about today's spotlight. It is mostly the word glow.
Browse by topic: MCP servers, coding agents, agent skills and more, each with a page of its own.
Deep cuts are projects outside the top 200 by stars: nearly all of the Atlas, and invisible if you sort by popularity.
Oh-Four got lost on the way here and found itself in the Catalogue. It says it's not lost. It's exploring.
Found something good? Star the original repository too. The maintainers see that; the Atlas is just the map.
The Shipped in the last seven days shelf is projects pushed within a week of the latest snapshot. Proof of life.
Quack asked Archie one question this morning: why? He's been explaining ever since. He's found three bugs.
Follow new arrivals from your feed reader: the Atlas publishes a feed of projects it has just added, newest first.
The Keep it honest collection is tools for checking what agents actually did, not just what they said they did.
Nib has opinions about kerning today. If a heading looks one letter lighter, that's Nib. It gives them back.
The Atlas comes in several skins. Try a new one today. Archie has a remark ready for every one of them.
The homepage keeps shelves by language, so the Rust and Go crowds can each find their own corner.
Posy left a reminder on Archie's visor: drink some water. It applies to you too. She insists.
Setting up a coding agent? The Claude Code kit collection is a good first shopping list.
The Catalogue's search runs in your browser, over an index the site ships with. Your queries stay on your machine.
Lumen is visiting again. Please don't tell her the spotlight is not the moon. She's having such a nice time.
Curious who has the most stars? The leaderboard lives in the Markdown mega-list on GitHub.
The Atlas re-reads its source lists regularly. Projects that were not there last time show up as new arrivals.
Oh-Four practised its boo all night. It is still more of an apologetic whisper. Be encouraging.
Shipping an agent? Observability and evals has the tools for seeing what it did and whether it did it well.
Archie claims he has read every README in the Atlas. He has read the first line of every README in the Atlas.
Quack is on call today. If Archie starts talking to himself, he isn't. He's talking to the duck.
Building something that has to remember? Context, memory and RAG is the topic to start with.
Archie's friends only visit now and then, and never while you're typing. If you saw one today, you were lucky.
Nib, Posy, Lumen, Oh-Four and Quack are all around today. Only one gets to visit. They drew straws. Nib cheated.
